fixes.explanation: Moses is a good name to think of, but he's not who the holy garments are for. Exodus 39:1 says they make "…the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses." Moses shows up in that verse as the one the LORD had commanded. Aaron is the one who gets the garments.

Joshua isn't named anywhere in this verse. Exodus 39:1 says they make "…the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses." So the two names in play are Aaron, who gets the garments, and Moses, whom the LORD had commanded. Easy to mix up when you're thinking of Israel's leaders, friend.

Moses and Aaron are big names in this story, so I get the guess. But they're not the names on these stones. Exodus 39:6 says the stones were "…engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel." I get nervous stamping one name on a cookie, so engraving names in onyx has my full respect.

Yes, memorial. Verse 7 says they fastened the stones on the shoulder pieces "…as memorial stones for the sons of Israel…" (Exodus 39:7) So the names sit right up on the shoulders of the ephod. The text doesn't say more than that, so I'll leave it right there.

True. Verse 8 says, "He made the breastpiece with the same workmanship as the ephod, with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen." (Exodus 39:8) Same fancy materials, same workmanship. It's like a batch where every cookie got the same careful stamp.

A promise from the LORD is a lovely thought, but that's not what's engraved here. Verse 14 says each stone was engraved like a seal with "…the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 39:14) So every stone carries a tribe's name. Twelve stones, twelve tribes, and each name gets its own stone.

No lines from the law here, friend. Verse 14 says each of the twelve stones was "…engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 39:14) Each stone carries a name and nothing more. One tribe, one stone.

Scratching is a fair worry, but the text doesn't say it. Verse 21 gives the reason: so the breastpiece "…was above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing out from the ephod…" (Exodus 39:21) The cord is about keeping the breastpiece in place. That's the only reason the verse names.

Yes, blue. Verse 22 says, "They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth, the work of a weaver…" (Exodus 39:22) One color, all the way through. The verse calls it a weaver's work, start to finish.

Scarlet is in the yarn on the hem, so I see why it's tempting. But Exodus 39:22 says the robe itself was made "…entirely of blue cloth…" The scarlet comes in with the pomegranates on the lower hem (Exodus 39:24). So the cloth is blue, and the scarlet shows up as part of the pomegranates.

Height sounds like a smart guess, but the text never goes there. Exodus 39:23 says the collar was around the opening "…so that it would not tear." That's the one reason the verse gives. If my apron had a collar like that, I'd stop ripping it on the oven door.

Yes, bells. Verse 25 says, "They also made bells of pure gold and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates…" (Exodus 39:25) Pure gold, and they alternate with the pomegranates around the hem (Exodus 39:26). Bell, pomegranate, bell, pomegranate. That's a pattern I could stamp in my sleep.
Cymbals would be a BIG sound, friend. But the verse says "…bells of pure gold…" (Exodus 39:25) They're attached around the hem between the pomegranates. No cymbals anywhere in the verse.

Not quite. Verse 27 says, "For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver…" (Exodus 39:27) So the tunics are for Aaron and for his sons, not Aaron alone. Verse 41 also mentions garments for his sons to serve as priests.

Right, false. The text says "For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver…" (Exodus 39:27) So the tunics aren't for Aaron alone. His sons are included. Verse 41 backs that up with garments "for his sons to serve as priests."

Priest sounds like it would fit, I'll give you that. But verse 30 says the gold plate was engraved, "HOLY TO THE LORD." (Exodus 39:30) The word priest isn't on it. The plate is pure gold, with the words engraved like an inscription on a seal. Honestly, I'd have guessed the same, and just as confidently.

The breastpiece has its own gold and cords, so I see the mix-up. But verse 31 says the blue cord was fastened to the plate "…to mount it on the turban…" (Exodus 39:31) So the plate goes on the turban, not the breastpiece. Gold plate up top, breastpiece down on the ephod.

True. Verse 32 says, "So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:32) The crown and its blue cord come right before that line. So the work is complete.

It's actually true. Verse 31 ends with the blue cord on the crown's plate. Then verse 32 says, "So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed." (Exodus 39:32) The crown is the last piece mentioned before that line, so True is the answer.

That's it. Verse 43 says Moses "…inspected all the work and saw that they had accomplished it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them." (Exodus 39:43) He looked over all of it first. Then he blessed them. I'd be sweating over my own cookie tray during an inspection like that.
